findings.rootCause: The first immutable run reported an ambiguous :compileJava console outcome. A diagnostic rerun passed all warm-up shapes and then found a byte difference in the required JAR. An isolated native-versus-selected reproduction found identical 80-entry ZIP structure and one changed payload: META-INF/groovy-release-info.properties embeds the wall-clock BuildTime.
findings.recoveryBoundary: BuildOpt may revisit this family only after the owner workflow emits a reproducible release-info payload or after an explicit owner-approved output contract replaces byte identity. It must not normalize the timestamp silently.

findings.rootCause: The Checkstyle XML report records absolute repository paths, so the isolated control and candidate workspaces cannot produce byte-identical reports even when the findings are the same.
findings.recoveryBoundary: A future owner-approved report contract may canonicalize only the isolated workspace prefix and must prove finding-level equality. The current exact-byte contract remains authoritative.

findings.rootCause: Kafka configures archives with reproducibleFileOrder=false and preserveFileTimestamps=true. Two consecutive native clean shadowJar builds had different archive SHA-256 values while all 4,378 entry names and every uncompressed payload were identical; ZIP timestamps changed.
findings.recoveryBoundary: BuildOpt may revisit this family when the owner makes the archive reproducible or explicitly approves a canonical archive-content contract. Exact bytes remain required today.

findings.rootCause: The installed candidate preserved exact class outputs and saved 2,695 ms on average, but only seven of eight preregistered pairs were positive. The frozen eight-of-eight repeatability gate therefore retained native Gradle.
findings.recoveryBoundary: Investigate the single negative observation and use a newly preregistered order-aware replication. Do not relax the completed gate after observing the result.
